newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Jakarta shares rebounded on Thursday on bargain-hunting of some heavyweight stocks and speculative buying of secondaries, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.34 points, or 0.59 percent, to 569.12 points after touching an intra-day low of 565.47 points in early trade. Advancers led decliners by 53 to 52, with 54 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the presence of bargain-hunters in the afternoon session had improved overall sentiment and they expected the market to be buoyant on Friday.
"But I think the index will move within a narrow range as a large number of local investors usually trade on a short-term basis," a broker from a major domestic firm said.
Property firm Bhuwanatala IP topped the active list with 18.6 million shares traded, gaining 275 rupiah to 1,500 rupiah. Brokers said it was due to talk the firm would link up with a Singaporea firm.
Ceramic producer Kedawung Setia rose 50 rupiah to 1,500 on a volume of 3.9 million shares on talk of possible cooperation with foreign parties.
Blue-chip telecommunications firm Telkom, satellite firm Indosat and cement maker Semen Gresik were among the targets of bargain-hunters, brokers said.
Car maker Astra International rose 3.18 percent to 4,050 rupiah on local-led buying after it dropped to 3,875 rupiah in early trade.

Sentiment on the stock had been weak following reports that Muhamad Hasan, who controls the Nusamba Group majority owned by foundations headed by President Suharto, was not interested in buying the automobile firm's shares if the price was too high, brokers said.
"But then in afternoon trade, some operators were actively buying the stock," said one foreign broker, adding that brokers believed Hasan had made the comments to allow prices to fall.
